title: Kingdom of Kent
capsule: The Kingdom of Kent was one of the earliest Anglo-Saxon kingdoms, established by Jutish settlers in southeastern Britain probably in the late fifth century under a dynasty claiming descent from the semi-legendary Hengist. It was the first English kingdom to receive Christian missionaries, with Augustine landing at Thanet in 597 at the invitation of King Æthelberht I, who became the first English king to accept baptism. At its height under Æthelberht, Kent exercised hegemony (bretwalda) over kingdoms south of the Humber. From the late seventh century Kent was repeatedly subordinated by Mercia and then Wessex; it was definitively absorbed into the Kingdom of Wessex under Ecgberht in 825–826.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Kent's political history is well attested in Bede, the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle, and contemporary charters; territorial extent corresponds closely to the Roman Cantium and is consistently documented.
